purpose: Investigate the three largest WebGPU Q8 versus BF16 differences; this is a numerical diagnostic, not a latency benchmark.

native.reference: Measured WebGPU Q8 probabilities and original BF16 token IDs
native.note: Differences are rounded to six decimal places by the native CLI. The initial exploratory 0.005 limit failed; the final run used the existing 0.03 Gemma validation limit, with no implementation changes.

fp32.note: Original BF16-stored weights loaded into FP32 arithmetic. No pack quantization. Timings were not used: the native diagnostic ran concurrently.

conclusion: Both quantized runtime arithmetic and original-weight arithmetic affect probabilities. Native/WebGPU Q8 agree on all three inspected decisions; this does not establish probability parity with the original checkpoint.
